# Sāmaṇḍaka Saṁyutta (SN 39)

**ID:** SN 39  
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Sāmaṇḍaka Saṁyutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0304m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāmaṇḍaka Saṁyutta* (SN 39) is the thirty-ninth section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated within the *Saḷāyatanavagga* [Bodhi 2003; Jennings 1948; Mrs. Rhys Davids 1927]. The chapter consists of sixteen discourses recording dialogues set at Ukkācelā (or Ukkāvelā) on the banks of the Ganges in the Vajjian country, where the wanderer (*paribbājaka*) Sāmaṇḍaka questions the Venerable Sāriputta [Bodhi 2003; Dhammika; Jennings 1948; Mrs. Rhys Davids 1927]. Sāmaṇḍaka's inquiries cover central doctrinal topics, such as the nature of *nibbāna* (defined by Sāriputta as the destruction of lust, hatred, and delusion), arahantship, the taints (*āsava*), the definition of suffering and happiness in terms of birth and non-birth, and the difficulty of practicing the Dhamma, with each answer extolling the Noble Eightfold Path as the way to realization [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994; Law 1931].

In structure and phrasing, this saṁyutta is practically identical to the preceding *Jambukhādaka Saṁyutta* (SN 38), differing only in the name of the wandering ascetic interlocutor [Bodhi 2003]. Because of this near-total correspondence, Pali manuscript traditions and printed editions heavily abridge the text, presenting the opening sutta and providing peyyāla instructions to expand the remaining discourses in parallel with SN 38 [Bodhi 2003].
